title: Dependency-aware launch grid and hotfix reserve process
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Past releases exposed a gap where parallel launches across runtime/console/api created hidden resource contention and left no fast path for urgent hotfixes. We need a repeatable, low-friction process to map component dependencies, reserve emergency capacity, and coordinate cutover windows with clear ownership.

Goals:
- Define a dependency-aware launch grid that captures service-level dependencies, regional capacity footprints, and rollback blast radius.
- Create an automated hotfix reserve allocation (initial target: 12% external capacity across three regions) and a lightweight request/approval flow.
- Produce runbook templates for staggered cutovers and pre-authorized hotfix activation to reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) by 30%.
- Ensure observability hooks (per-route token cost, latency heatmap) are surfaced in the launch playbook for real-time go/no-go decisions.

Scope: runtime, console, and public API surfaces for any release that changes serving runtime kernels, routing policies, or Console rollout behavior. Does not include data-plane infra changes (separate change control).

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in mean time to mitigation for launch-caused incidents in Q2.
- Hotfix reserve activation time <= 15 minutes from approval.
- 95% of launches have validated dependency graph in the launch grid before Goodbye-to-Production signoff.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical launch grid document exists in Confluence and is linked from the release ticket.
Automated script tags nodes in capacity manager and reserves hotfix pool (config flag) in three regions.
Runbook templates (staggered cutover + hotfix activation) are approved by SRE and Product.
Dashboard widgets added: per-route latency spike alert and reserve-utilization gauge.
Two pilot launches use the new grid and hotfix reserve; postmortems show improved mitigation times.
tasks: Map current dependency graph for runtime/console/api services (ENG + SRE) and validate with owners.
Prototype hotfix reserve allocator: CLI and Console toggle to set reserve percentage by region.
Design launch grid template (CSV + auto-generated visualization) with flags: rollback_owner, blast_radius, reserve_required.
Integrate a preflight validator in the release checklist that ensures dependencies are annotated and reserve configured.
Run two staged pilot launches and capture telemetry for evaluation.

notes: Decision log: prefer automated reserve allocation over manual ops tickets to reduce latency and human error.
Risk: mis-estimating reserve size could throttle customer traffic; mitigations: canary reserve drain test and automated rollback by threshold.
Trade-offs: conservative reserve reduces outage risk but increases cost; optional cost offset proposal: temporary token-budget increase for affected customers during launch windows.
Postmortem action from INCIDENT-2025-11: add per-route token-level tracing to speed root cause identification; included in acceptance criteria.
Follow-ups: consider surfacing reserve consumption in public status page for enterprise customers during major launches.
